title: Check acceptance criteria and accessibility
summary: Before anything goes to users, check it does what the stories promised and that disabled people can use it. Accessibility is a legal duty for many services, and fixing problems late costs far more.

beginner: For each story, go through its acceptance criteria one by one in a test environment. Mark each as passed or failed, and raise a bug for each failure.
Ask your tester or engineers to run an automated accessibility checker. Automated tools only catch part of the problems, so this is a starting point.
Do a basic manual check yourself: use the feature with only a keyboard, zoom the page to 200%, and check text is readable and every button says what it does.
Ask someone to try it with a screen reader, such as VoiceOver on a Mac or iPhone, or NVDA on Windows.
Agree with the team which problems must be fixed before release and which can wait. Write down any that wait, with a date.
Before release, record the result: what was tested, what passed and what is still known to be wrong.
intermediate: Test every story against its acceptance criteria and log failures as bugs.
Run automated accessibility checks plus manual checks: keyboard only, zoom and screen reader.
Triage issues with the team into 'must fix before release' and 'known issues'.
Record the test outcome and update the accessibility statement if you have one.
experienced: Verify all acceptance criteria, and log and triage failures.
Check WCAG 2.2 AA with automated and manual testing, including assistive technology.
Get release-blocking issues fixed, and record known issues with dates.
Update the accessibility statement where one is required.

canDelegateTo.task: Test each story against its criteria and run accessibility checks
Add automated accessibility tests and fix issues found
Test with disabled users and people who use assistive technology
Check headings, labels, link text and error messages are clear

toolExamples.jira: Link each bug to the story it came from, and use a label such as 'accessibility' so you can report on those issues separately.
toolExamples.azure-devops: Use Test Plans to record a pass or fail against each acceptance criterion.
toolExamples.github: Ask engineers to run an automated accessibility check on every pull request, so problems are caught before they merge.
toolExamples.confluence: Keep a test summary page per release: what was tested, results and known issues.
toolExamples.claude: Paste your acceptance criteria and ask which ones are hard to test as written and how to reword them.

definitionOfDone: Every acceptance criterion tested and marked passed or failed
Automated and manual accessibility checks done, including a screen reader
Known issues written down with a plan to fix them
pitfalls: Relying only on automated accessibility tools
Leaving accessibility until the end of the project

sources.title: Accessibility guidance for product and delivery (NHS digital service manual)
